f.title: PSUR/PBRER content objectives
f.statement: The PSUR/PBRER presents the worldwide safety experience of the product at defined times in order to: report all relevant new information from appropriate sources; relate the data to patient exposure; summarise the authorisation status in different countries and significant safety-related variations; periodically re-evaluate overall safety; give a concise evaluation of benefit unless the profile has changed significantly; and indicate whether product information changes are needed.
f.applicability: MAHs and Local Representatives of regulated products granted marketing authorization in Ghana (FDA Guidelines on Safety Monitoring of Medicinal Products, FDA/SMD/GDL-04/03)

rows.actor: Local Representative or Marketing Authorization Holder
rows.quote: PSUR/PBRER presents the worldwide safety experience of a medicinal product at defined times post authorization, in order to: a. Report all the relevant new information from appropriate sources; b. Relate these data to patient exposure; c. Summarize the market authorization status in different countries and any significant variations related to safety; d. Create periodically the opportunity for an overall safety re-evaluation; e. Provide a formal and concise evaluation of benefit, unless the safety or benefit risk profile has changed significantly during the reporting interval. f. Indicate whether changes should be made to product information in order to optimize the use of the product.
rows.review_note: Review: objectives clause with no modal; read as Recommended content expectations. Double-check: confirmed.

f.statement: Safety communication should be effective - transmitted, received and understood by the target audience as intended, with appropriate action taken - and systems should be put in place to measure its effectiveness.

f.title: Include required content in safety communications
f.statement: Safety communication should contain: important emerging information affecting benefit-risk; the reason for the communication; recommendations to healthcare professionals and patients; where applicable, a statement of MAH-Authority agreement; information on proposed product information changes; literature references or where to find more detail; and, where relevant, a reminder to report suspected adverse reactions.
